Who was the last Asaf Jahi (Nizam) ruler?
x:
Mir Osman Ali Khan (Asaf Jah VII) was the last Nizam of Hyderabad and the seventh ruler of the Asaf Jahi dynasty. He ruled from 1911 to 1948 and was one of the wealthiest rulers in the world during his time. After India attained independence in 1947, Osman Ali Khan initially refused to accede to the Indian Union and attempted to maintain Hyderabad as an independent state. This led to Operation Polo (Police Action) in September 1948, through which the Government of India integrated Hyderabad State into the Indian Union. Following the integration, Osman Ali Khan remained the Rajpramukh of Hyderabad State until the reorganization of states.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).
n: Last Nizam – Mir Osman Ali Khan

s: Who was the founder of the Asaf Jahi Dynasty in the Deccan?
x:
The Asaf Jahi Dynasty was founded by Mir Qamar-ud-din Khan, popularly known as Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I, in 1724 CE. Initially appointed as the Mughal Governor of the Deccan by Emperor Farrukhsiyar, he defeated Mubariz Khan in the Battle of Shakar Kheda (1724) and established an independent state with Hyderabad as its centre. The Asaf Jahi rulers governed Hyderabad until 1948, when Hyderabad State was integrated into the Indian Union after Operation Polo.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (2).
